constitutive_assumptions: The honeycomb structure in its initial state is simplified geometrically as a rectangular block.
Only the outer thick-wall structure and the string length are accounted for in the kinematic deformation model, excluding the low-modulus thin-walled inner honeycomb cells.
Strings are assumed to lie at the top surface of the honeycomb structure with a constant initial height during deformation.
Structural deformation upon center indentation is assumed to be symmetric between the left and right sides.
The indenter is assumed to press down completely to the bottom of the honeycomb structure.
The lateral side-wall deformation contour of the structure is assumed to bend with a constant radius of curvature.
Applied external contact forces and dynamic structural effects are not considered in the geometric deformation angle model.
control_variables: Initial pressing force (set to 20 N for macroscale shape adaptation tests)
Initial pressing distance (set to 15 mm for mesoscale position dependency tests)
Geometry and material modulus of internal spring units (outer diameter 5 mm, inner diameter 4 mm, free length 25 mm; vertical modulus 22.7 kPa, lateral modulus 3.05 MPa)
Gripper base dimensions and string layer count (10 parallel strings)
dependent_variables: Gripping weight capacity and holding force
Converging deformation angle and edge displacement / height
Elastic modulus of the stiffness-variable shell structure (under different jamming states and directional forces)
Contact sealing completeness (evaluated via ink transfer patterns)
Task execution success (bin picking, hammering, calligraphy, breakfast preparation, plug insertion/removal, vaccination)

evidence_relevant_to_topic.claim: Combining macroscale structure deformation with mesoscale cell adaptation enables suction sealing and grasping on highly irregular, non-planar surfaces.

Orthotropic surface tension produced by embedded unidirectional strings governs directional deformation, where perpendicular orientation enhances convex object enclosing and parallel orientation enhances concave adaptation.
Negative-pressure particle jamming in an outer shell increases structural stiffness, preventing pose deflection under external loads during dynamic tasks like hammering and calligraphy.
Unsealed hexagonal cells lead to vacuum leakage, significantly diminishing gripping performance when grasping objects smaller than a cell or porous substrates.

experimental_setup: 3D optical scanner setup measuring surface deformation profiles, converging distances, and angles under central and dual-edge rod indentation.

Force measurement test bench evaluating gripping weight and pull-off force across object shapes (cylindrical, rectangular prism, triangular prism, concave, thin plate, hyperelastic balls) at varied sizes and offsets.
Ink stamp transfer printing to observe individual hexagonal cell sealing boundaries on irregular target surfaces without air leakage.
Mechanical stiffness testing apparatus applying external loads in four directions on a gripped rectangular bar to evaluate modulus changes between jamming ON and OFF states.

Robotic manipulator setup demonstrating bin-picking of 14 unregistered stacked objects and complex manipulation tasks (hammering, calligraphy, breakfast preparation, cord unplugging/plugging, vaccination).
future_work: Development of an active mechanism capable of dynamically modulating the effective contact surface area of the gripper in real time to accommodate thin and small objects.
Development of a finite element method (FEM) model incorporating nonlinear large deformation and anisotropic material properties to predict gripper mechanics.
independent_variables: Surface tension orientation relative to object longitudinal axis (high surface tension / perpendicular alignment vs. low surface tension / parallel alignment)
Jamming state of the stiffness-variable structure (jamming ON with negative pressure vs. jamming OFF vs. without jamming)
Target object geometry (convex, concave, thin plate, spherical, cylindrical, prismatic) and size/width
Offset position of the target object relative to the gripper centerline
Direction of applied external disturbance force (four orientations)
limitations_inferred: The fixed orientation of the embedded strings requires pre-aligning the gripper with the principal axis of the target object to achieve optimal convex or concave adaptation.
Activating macroscale adaptation requires substantial pre-pressing force (e.g., 20 N), which may damage fragile, brittle, or highly compliant objects.
Pneumatic actuation of both distributed suction and granular jamming may increase cycle times during release due to the need to vent multiple vacuum chambers.
Long-term cyclic fatigue and durability of internal strings, lateral-support springs, and elastomeric membranes were not evaluated.
limitations_stated_by_authors: Relatively low gripping force when handling small and thin objects due to air leakage through unoccupied, open hexagonal holes.
Inability to grip objects smaller than a single hexagonal cell (such as thin wire) or air-permeable porous surfaces (such as mesh).
Lower gripping force on flat surfaces compared to conventional industrial suction cups.
main_results: The orthotropic surface tension mechanism achieved large inward converging deformation (up to 69 degrees) for convex objects and effective elongation (up to 40 degrees) for concave objects.
High surface tension orientation maintained full gripping capacity even with up to a 10 percent center offset on convex targets.
Ink transfer confirmed complete mesoscale sealing along sharp edges and vertical walls, preventing air leakage across individual hexagonal chambers.

The particle-jamming stiffness-variable shell increased modulus by 5.35 times in the jammed state and maintained rigidity by 1.39 to 2.37 times against external multi-directional forces, supporting tilted 4 kg loads.
Demonstrated versatile performance in complex multi-step manipulation tasks including hammering nails, brush calligraphy, meal serving, unregistered bin-picking, and simulated vaccination.
modeling_methods: Analytical kinematic/geometric model relating string elongation ratio, side-wall constant radius of curvature, and top surface deformation angle during center indentation.
performance_metrics: Deformation angle (degrees) and inward edge converging distance (mm)
Modulus enhancement ratio (5.35x increase from unjammed to jammed; 1.39x to 2.37x under multi-directional external disturbance forces)
Offset tolerance percentage without loss of gripping capacity (up to 10%)
Spring structure directional modulus (22.7 kPa vertical vs. 3.05 MPa lateral)
possible_gap_implications: The vulnerability to vacuum loss from uncovered cells indicates a fundamental challenge in passive distributed suction arrays, suggesting that autonomous cell-level valving or area-throttling mechanisms are necessary for open-ended object sorting.
The dependence on string orientation suggests that reconfigurable or multi-axial surface tension structures could remove the requirement for rotational pre-alignment prior to contact.
paper.research_objective: To develop an all-round universal honeycomb suction gripper utilizing orthotropic surface tension for two-level (macroscale and mesoscale) shape adaptation inspired by octopus tentacles, combined with a particle-jamming stiffness-variable structure to securely hold gripped objects against external forces during complex manipulation tasks.
paper.research_problem: Conventional astrictive vacuum suction grippers experience dramatic loss of adhesive force when handling complex, non-flat, or irregular surfaces due to air leakage at grooves, bumps, and holes, while also lacking the mechanical rigidity needed to maintain grasp stability under external forces during tool use and complex tasks.
paper.robot_type: Universal honeycomb suction gripper (astrictive-type soft gripper)
stiffness_mechanism: Orthotropic spring-string structure (embedded lateral-modulus springs and unidirectional strings)
paper.title: Highly Shape-Adaptable Honeycomb Gripper Using Orthotropic Surface Tension
